# 1. Executive Snapshot

- **Frontier-model prices fell again.** Claude Opus 5.5 (released Sept 22) lists $4/$20 per million input/output tokens, down from $5/$25 for Opus 5, with cache reads at $0.20/M and Batch at 50% off. Anthropic's platform docs match these figures; other details come from blogs. Yesterday's cache-pricing item moves from "unverified" to "largely confirmed".
- **OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol (heavy) and Luna (high-volume) launched on Amazon Bedrock the same day as OpenAI's own announcement**, reportedly at lower prices than GPT-5.6 (AWS blog; exact prices not confirmed). Two top vendors now sell through the same cloud marketplace, which makes switching cheaper.
- **Opportunity:** a tiered model design (Luna-class for routing and extraction, Opus/Sol-class for hard tasks) combined with caching and batch can plausibly cut inference spend materially. We have not measured this.
- **Risk:** Opus 5.5 defaults to medium reasoning effort and always-on adaptive thinking. A blog lists breaking changes versus Opus 5 (unverified). Silent behavior change on upgrade is a regression risk for any workflow we have in production. Governance remains the open item for the thirteenth report.
- **Recommended attention level: Medium.** Act on the cost model and the agent-control standard. Vercel Ship SF is on Oct 15; no launches are announced yet.

# 2. Technologies Worth Watching

**Technology:** Claude Opus 5.5 (pricing, effort defaults, 1M context)

**Category:** AI / Cost

**What happened?**
Released Sept 22 as the first 5.5-family model. $4/$20 per M tokens, cache reads $0.20/M, 50% batch discount, 1M input / 128K output, default effort "medium", available on the Claude API, Bedrock, Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry. Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 were said to follow within weeks. Pricing and date match Anthropic docs; the rest is secondary. Note: the "40% cheaper to run at default settings" claim reflects lower reasoning effort, not just list price, so it is workload-dependent.

**Why it matters?**
Cost per task depends on three things: list price, reasoning effort, and cache hit rate. Upgrading without measuring may change both quality and spend.

**Business Value:** Lower inference cost for agent and long-context work; possible quality gains.

**Company Relevance:** 80

**Priority:** High

**Recommendation:** Pilot (A/B one workflow against its current model at default and raised effort; record cost per successful task)

**Expected Impact:** Short

**Technology:** GPT-6 Sol / Luna on Amazon Bedrock

**Category:** AI / Cloud

**What happened?**
AWS's ML blog reports both models generally available on Bedrock, with up to 1M context and lower API prices than GPT-5.6. Sol targets coding and multistep work; Luna targets summarization, extraction, classification and routing with per-request reasoning effort. Bedrock ID reported as `openai.gpt-6-sol` (us-east-1). Same-day Bedrock availability is sourced to AWS plus a developer blog; the exact prices were not checked.

**Why it matters?**
If we are on AWS, one account, one IAM and billing surface can now reach both major vendors. That reduces the cost of building the multi-vendor abstraction and the eval comparison already on our list.

**Business Value:** Vendor leverage; simpler procurement and data-governance review.

**Company Relevance:** 65 (higher if we run on AWS)

**Priority:** Medium

**Recommendation:** Pilot (include Luna as the cheap tier in the Haiku-class cost comparison that is still open)

**Expected Impact:** Medium

**Technology:** Reasoning-effort as a cost knob

**Category:** AI / Engineering

**What happened?**
Both Opus 5.5 (default medium, previously high) and GPT-6 Luna (adjustable per request) expose effort as a parameter.

**Why it matters?**
Effort is now a per-request budget decision. A routing layer that picks model and effort per task type is a concrete cost lever and needs evals to set safely.

**Business Value:** Spend control without changing vendors.

**Company Relevance:** 70

**Priority:** Medium

**Recommendation:** Pilot (fold into the model eval set)

**Expected Impact:** Short-Medium

# 3. New Tools & Platforms

**Tool:** Anthropic Batch API + prompt caching (existing, now cheaper)

**Category:** AI / Operations

**What does it do?**
Batch gives 50% off for non-urgent jobs; cache reads cost $0.20/M on Opus 5.5 versus $4 for fresh input.

**Who should use it?**
Whoever owns nightly or bulk jobs: report generation, classification, code review sweeps, document processing.

**Business Use Case:** Move every non-interactive LLM job to batch and restructure prompts so stable content comes first.

**Estimated ROI:** Potentially large on eligible workloads (up to 50% from batch alone, more with cache hits); needs measurement on our traffic.

**Recommended Experiment:** Pick the highest-volume non-interactive job, run it for a week in batch with a cache-friendly prompt layout, compare cost and output quality.

**Estimated Evaluation Time:** 2 days

---

**Tool:** Amazon Bedrock multi-vendor access (Claude and GPT-6 via one API surface)

**Category:** Cloud / AI

**What does it do?**
Serves models from several vendors under one AWS account, IAM and billing.

**Who should use it?**
Platform and security leads if we are already on AWS.

**Business Use Case:** Run the same eval set against both vendors without new contracts or data-processing reviews.

**Estimated ROI:** Medium; saves procurement and integration time, and gives price leverage.

**Recommended Experiment:** Enable two models in a sandbox account, run 20 real tasks from the planned eval set, compare cost and pass rate.

**Estimated Evaluation Time:** 3 days

# 4. Global Technology Direction

**Where is the market moving?**

- **Price per unit of useful work is falling through three channels at once:** lower list prices (Opus 5.5, GPT-6), cheaper reuse (cache reads, batch), and tunable effort. Capability headlines matter less than whether we can use these channels.
- **Distribution is converging on hyperscaler marketplaces.** Frontier models from competing labs appear on Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry on launch day. Model choice is becoming a configuration, not a contract.
- **Release cadence is quick and naming is unstable** (5.5 family, GPT-6 Sol/Luna/Astra, Gemini 4 expected before year-end). Any design pinned to one model name will churn.

**Strategic implications:** Advantage goes to teams with an eval set, a routing layer and cost telemetry. Those let us adopt each release in days rather than weeks and renegotiate from evidence.

## What This Means For Our Company

1. Build the eval set first; it is the prerequisite for every other model decision on our list.
2. Measure cost per successful task, not per token. Effort defaults changed, so old benchmarks are stale.
3. Do not commit to long single-vendor terms while prices are falling this fast.
4. Hold any production upgrade to Opus 5.5 until the Opus 5 breaking-change list is checked in Anthropic's release notes.
